26          THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

with more mathematics. Also a very practical “diploma course,” (described in a later catalog), stripped of lan-guages and higher mathematics, was undoubtedly available that year and probably from the time of the charter.

    The schedule for the B.S. degree, which was advertised without modification for the three years, 1885-1888, was as follows:

B.S.

FRESHMAN YEAR

        Higher Arithmetic and Algebra
        Latin Grammar, Reader, Caesar
        French or German
        Rhetoric

SOPHOMORE YEAR

        Geometry, Trigonometry, Surveying
        Virgil, Cicero
        French or German
        Physiology
        Physics

JUNIOR YEAR

        Navigation, Conic Sections, Analytical Geometry
        Horace, Livy
        Chemistry
        Elocution

SENIOR YEAR

        Calculus, Astronomy
        Political Economy
        Evidences of Christianity
        Mental Science, Moral Science
        Mineralogy

    EVOLUTION OF THE A.B. DEGREE.—The course for the A.B. degree shows a notable evolution from 1885 to 1888. As published in 1885-1886, its requirements were:

FRESHMAN YEAR

        Higher Arithmetic and University Algebra
        Latin Grammar, Reader, Caesar
        Greek Grammar, Reader, Xenophon’s Anabasis
        Rhetoric
